$comment: Hand-owned editorial layer for proofs.mino.mobi, one entry per family of the openai/math release. Seeded 2026-10-06 by six model readers against one rubric (A = computable widget, B = illustrative, C = card only); every A needs a human look before building. `page` is the built widget path, relative to proofs/. build.mjs joins this with the release itself.

001.widget: Text card on Hodge classes on abelian varieties and reduction mod p; nothing finite to compute.
001.hook: why algebraic cycles are hard to find

002.widget: Text card on BSD: rank, Sha and the leading-term formula, perhaps with a table of curves.
002.hook: A Millennium Prize problem settled for most curves

003.widget: Plot |L(s,chi)| and zeros of zeta/Dirichlet L-functions over the critical strip with the proven zero-free half-plane Re s>7/8 shaded against RH's line 1/2.
003.hook: first unconditional zero-free half-plane for zeta beyond Re s=1

004.widget: Text card on why deciding rational solvability of polynomial equations is impossible, beside the integer (Matiyasevich) case.
004.hook: No algorithm can tell if an equation has a fraction solution

005.widget: Compute G to 600 digits two independent ways, see the 0.0000999 gap between the two bounds that rules out a fraction, plot the barrier functions with every root bracket, and replay both of the paper's finite certificates.
005.engine: BigInt rationals and 60-digit fixed-point logs: rebuilds the trial numerators (degrees 36/24/13/9), Descartes counts and all 43 root brackets, all 50 certified values and the final bound -2.290939875; rebuilds the 49×48 matrix ℬ from its recipe, matches all 144 mod-101 pivots, and computes the three 48×48 determinants exactly over ℚ.
005.hook: a famous constant finally proved irrational

006.widget: Text card: quadratic twists of an elliptic curve split 50/50 between analytic rank 0 and 1; at most a root-number parity tally.
006.hook: half of all twisted curves have no rational points of infinite order

007.widget: Plot the Liouville function's two-point correlation sum sum lambda(n)lambda(n+h) (and along other affine forms) up to X ~ 10^7 against X/(log X)^c, showing the cancellation the theorem proves.
007.hook: primes' parity looks like coin flips, even in pairs

008.widget: Text card on the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra and its free odd generators.
008.hook: Hidden symmetry of multiple zeta values

009.widget: Text card on recovering a function field from its mod-l Milnor K-groups (anabelian reconstruction).

010.widget: Card explaining modularity of 2-adic Galois representations.
010.hook: Last piece of Fontaine-Mazur in dimension two

011.widget: Sample primes p, factor p-1, and compare the ordered log-sizes of its prime factors against the Poisson-Dirichlet PD(1) law; also explore large totient fibers.
011.hook: how p-1 breaks into primes is as random as a random permutation's cycles

012.widget: Scatter log P+(n)/log n against log P+(n+1)/log(n+1) for n up to ~10^7 and watch the joint histogram approach a product of two Dickman densities; live tally of P+(n)<P+(n+1).
012.hook: is the biggest prime factor of n a coin-flip relative to n+1?

013.widget: Pick two small sets A, B and watch A+B against the primes: a sandbox showing why sumsets develop structure (residue classes, gaps) that the primes lack.
013.hook: the primes cannot be split as a sum of two sets

014.widget: Text card on restricted geometric Langlands over finite fields.

015.widget: Animate CM/Heegner-type torus orbits on the modular surface filling it uniformly as the discriminant grows (degree-2 analogue of the packets).
015.hook: arithmetic orbits spread evenly over a curved space

016.widget: Card on unlikely intersections in abelian varieties and A2.

017.widget: Explore continued fractions of pi: plot q^2|pi - p/q| for convergents and the partial sums of the Flint-Hills series sum 1/(n^3 sin^2 n).
017.hook: pi cannot be approximated unusually well by fractions; Flint-Hills converges

018.widget: Text card on normal subgroups of arithmetic groups (Margulis--Platonov).

088.widget: Drag a polygon and watch its projection body (K - K turned a quarter turn) and R2 between 4 and 6; turn solids and their zonotope projection bodies between the ball (3pi^2/4) and the tetrahedron (18); recompute the 20-dimensional counterexample T10 x T10 from its 22 facet vectors; map every product T_r x T_s and the best product of simplices in each dimension against Petty's ellipsoid minimum.
088.engine: Exact BigInt zonotope volumes (sum of |det| over d-subsets of facet area-normals, Bareiss): 231 determinants of 20x20 give 22355476/22020096 without the product formula, which is also checked on 13 other products; simplex value from the facet zonotope to d = 12; dynamic programming over splits into simplices (first win at n = 20, exact recheck to 30); planar and spatial facet lemma against measured shadows; brute-force 3D hulls and zonotope faces for drawing. Petty's n >= 4 inequality is analysis and only illustrated.

089.widget: Draw a planar graph, compute its shortest-path metric and a cut-metric (L1) embedding via LP on small instances, and show the distortion.

090.widget: Compare energy per particle of the triangular lattice against square and random planar configurations for Gaussian/Riesz potentials, and replay the finite certificate behind its universal optimality.
090.engine: Recomputes the atomic certificate's finite blocks (two 20x20 matrices, parameter-polytope bounds, Bernstein tables) in interval arithmetic, plus lattice theta-sum energies; optionally the sharp Fourier packing certificate (coefficients.tsv, W_plus/W_minus.tsv) giving density pi/sqrt(12).
